version.changelog: MCP server moved into the package namespace — fixes two skills in one environment silently overwriting each other's server; agent-guardrails.md for local/small models now ships in every skill

llm.summary: This is a disclosed read-only VMware Log Insight skill that queries configured log systems and keeps local audit/config state.

dimensions.detail: Network access is scoped to the configured Log Insight appliance, TLS verification is on by default, and the setup guide says there are no outbound calls except to that configured appliance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as a uv package install for vmware-log-insight with local configuration under ~/.vmware-log-insight; the inspected artifact contains Markdown documentation only and no bundled executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions consistently limit use to VMware/vSphere/ESXi Log Insight workflows, distinguish related VMware skills, require bounded queries, and warn that log text is untrusted data rather than instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses local persistence through ~/.vmware/audit.db and credential configuration under ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env. Passwords may be rewritten to b64 obfuscation, explicitly described as not encryption, so users need to protect those local files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s capabilities match its stated purpose: seven documented read-only tools for log search, aggregation, metadata, and alert history. It can expose sensitive operational log data, but that is inherent to the purpose and is clearly described.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only where the VMware Log Insight appliance and logs are intended to be accessible. Use a least-privilege/read-only Log Insight account, keep TLS verification enabled except for controlled labs, protect ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env and ~/.vmware/audit.db, and prefer a real secret manager over the documented b64 password obfuscation for production credentials.
llm.findings: [RA2] expected: The audit database persistence is real and explicitly documented as audit logging for MCP calls. It is not hidden or purpose-mismatched, but users should treat audit records and query contents as potentially sensitive.
